newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson defends consent for Great Western.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson defends consent for Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co said it believes its consent solicitation is a true vote for Great Western Financial Corp shareholders and does not hurt or limit any other offers that might come in.
"It gets the process going," said a spokeswoman in response to an earlier statement by Great Western, in which it urged shareholders not to participate in the consent solicitation.
Earlier, Great Western urged shareholders not to sign the consent solicitation, which it said would limit the board's options and flexibility in evaluating Ahmanson's proposal.

One of Ahmanson's proposed bi-law amendments would preclude the Great Western board from attracting other potential bidders. Sources have said Great Western is involved in exploratory discussions with other banks, including Washington Mutual Savings Bank. Both banks have declined comment on the speculation, but Washington Mutual's chief executive Kerry Killinger said Tuesday he was ready to consider further acquisitions.

Ahmanson said Great Western's assertion that the consent solicitation was an attempt to limit Great Western's flexiblity amounted to "further obfuscation." A spokesman said if the Great Western board acted in a reasonable way, the consent soliciation would not affect the outcome.

In response to a claim by Great Western that shareholders were being pressured to make a hasty decision, the Ahmanson spokesman said two and a half weeks had passed since the Ahmanson bid was announced. "We think that's a reasonable amount of time," he said.
The Ahmanson spokesman said about four weeks would have elapsed by the time the consent solitication was completed.
